newsitem.title: MACAU: Air Macau to start service to Manila on July 21.
newsitem.headline: Air Macau to start service to Manila on July 21.

text.p: Air Macau said on Thursday it will start twice-weekly service to Manila from July 21, four days after the governor of the Portuguse-run enclave signs an air services agreement with the Philippines.
The service to Manila on Mondays and Fridays will bring the number of scheduled flights operated by Air Macau to 103 per week, the airline said.
Air Macau now flies to the Chinese cities of Beijing, Shanghai, Xiamen, Wuhan, Qingdao and Xiamen, as well as Taipei and Kaohsiung in Taiwan and the Thai capital, Bangkok.
The airline plans to launch scheduled flights to the southern Japanese city of Fukuoka later this year.

Air Macau is owned 14 percent by casino operator Sociedade De Turismo e Diversoes de Macau, 51 percent by China state-owned Air China, 25 percent by TAP-Air Portugal, five percent by the Macau government and five percent by other investors.
